sections.skill: Find the true cost of subscriptions and compare service plans

questions.prompt: Jamal has three streaming services at $15.99 each per month. What do they cost in a year?
questions.intro: Small monthly charges add up. Yearly cost = monthly cost × 12.
questions.topic: Subscriptions, free trials, and phone plans

misconceptions.B: Counts one service for a year
misconceptions.A: Gives one month for all three

sources: FTC (Negative option and automatic renewal offers): Free trials and subscriptions often renew automatically and charge a card on file unless canceled; consumers should note renewal dates and how to cancel. questions.prompt: A free 7-day trial requires a card and converts to $12.99 a month. Jamal wants only the trial. What should he do?

choices.text: Assume trials end on their own
Sign up twice to get a longer free trial
Set a reminder to cancel before day 7

questions.correct_answer: Set a reminder to cancel before day 7
questions.intro: Many free trials automatically become paid subscriptions. Note the end date and how to cancel when you sign up.
questions.feedback: Cancel before the trial ends to avoid charges.

questions.prompt: Plan A: $45 a month, unlimited data. Plan B: $25 a month plus $10 per GB. At how many GB a month do the plans cost the same?
questions.intro: Set the costs equal: 25 + 10g = 45. Below that amount, Plan B is cheaper; above it, Plan A is.

questions.prompt: Plan A: $45 a month, unlimited data. Plan B: $25 a month plus $10 per GB. Jamal uses about 6 GB a month. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
questions.feedback: Plan B: $25 + 6 × $10 = $85. Plan A: $45. A is $40 less.
